videos.title: ChatGPT Enterprise at Zendesk: Putting Company Data to Work
videos.description:
“We have about 600 applications that have been built by different people in the company.”

At Zendesk, teams across sales, marketing, and operations are building applications for their own work. ChatGPT Enterprise is available to every employee, and business users are asking questions about their data directly.

In sales, an AI agent connects product usage and tickets per agent to surface expansion opportunities—and helps salespeople explain how the customer could benefit. About 1,000 people use the application every day.

Watch Daniel Humble, VP of Enterprise Data and Analytics at Zendesk, share what teams are building and putting to work.

videos.title: Model a Game Asset From Concept to Engine | Part 4: Texture Baking in 3ds Max
videos.description:
Every game world is built one asset at a time! 🔥 Join 3D artist James Brady as he brings his sci-fi fire hydrant one step closer to game-ready by baking high-res textures onto his optimized low-poly model using Autodesk 3ds Max.

🚀 In Part 4, James brings his UV-unwrapped model from Maya back into 3ds Max to begin the texture baking process. Follow along as he sets up texture maps, adjusts the projection cage, and transfers details from the high-poly model to the low-poly asset. See how he applies and previews the baked textures, including normal, ambient occlusion, metallic, and roughness maps, to preserve visual detail while keeping the geometry optimized for game performance.

🎮 What's next? With the textures baked and applied, follow along as James takes the next steps toward bringing his sci-fi fire hydrant into Unreal Engine 5. Whether you're building props, environments, or your next sci-fi game world, discover how using different tools available in the Autodesk Media & Entertainment Collection can help you bring your assets from concept to engine.

videos.title: Houdini 22 | How to Deform Crowds with ML
videos.description:
Lesson Files: 

Learn how to apply a trained ML Deformer to crowd agents in Houdini to create more realistic skin deformation. You’ll explore the trained machine learning model and its supporting data, then use them to enhance character deformation during crowd animation.

You’ll also explore how ML Deformer improves upon traditional linear blend skinning, helping artists achieve more natural character movement and higher quality deformations across animated crowds.

videos.title: Houdini 22 | How to Utilize Shotsculpt
videos.description:
Lesson FIles: https://www.sidefx.com/tutorials/how-to-utilize-shotsculpt/

Learn how to use the new Shot Sculpt features in Houdini 22 to deform both polygonal geometry and hair guide curves directly in the viewport. You’ll explore how to sculpt and manage deformations over time while keeping hair guides attached to the underlying skin.

You’ll also explore the new Sculpt, Attribute, and Blend Shape modes for creating animated deformations, painting attributes, and blending between different shapes. These improvements give artists greater flexibility when refining character animation, adding secondary motion, and managing time dependent changes to geometry and grooms.

videos.title: Houdini 22 | How to Set a Following Camera
videos.description:
Project Files: https://www.sidefx.com/tutorials/how-to-set-a-following-camera/

Learn how to create a tracking camera in Houdini 22 using the new camera primitives. You’ll attach a camera to a selected point on an animated character and adjust its position and viewing angle while keeping it connected to the character’s movement.

You’ll also explore how to use Camera from Points and Camera Edit to create a follow camera for inspecting character details, reviewing Shot Sculpt edits, and identifying hair intersections during animation. This workflow gives artists a simple and flexible way to closely examine moving characters and refine their work.
